notes:
Mercedes-Benz C-Class W204 (saloon, estate and C204 coupe), GLK X204 and E-Class W212 (saloon and estate), the powertrain units.

Two sources. The first is a CAN database in the open ultimate-nag52 transmission firmware (GPL-3.0), whose header names its source file 204_POWERTRAIN_SB.dat: the W204 powertrain sub-bus. It gives the diagnostic request and response frames of the TCM, FSCM, ISM, SSP and TSLM, a functional KWP2000 request on 0x440 and a functional UDS request on 0x441, so the platform carries units of both protocols. It lists the requests under the engine control unit, which suggests the engine module relays them onto that sub-bus; whether the socket sends the same identifiers is not stated, and only the TCM's is backed by a response record.

The second is the OBDb response records (CC-BY-SA-4.0; only the request header, response header and service are used here, never a signal definition), each the request and reply a car returned to an OBDb user, filed by US model year. They show the engine and transmission answering at 0x7E0 and 0x7E1 on a 2014 C-Class, a 2014 E-Class and a 2012 GLK, which OBDb's generation dates place in W204, W212 and X204. The model year is all the records say about the car; no market, engine or VIN.

The protocol and session are KWP2000 and 0x92, as in mercedes-w211, and are not established for every unit: the 2012 GLK's transmission answered KWP2000 service 21, while the 2014 E-Class transmission and both 2014 engines answered only the two-byte identifiers of service 22. A unit that refuses 10 92 is reported in its scan notes.

Left out: the 0x7E2 brake unit and 0x7E5 unit OBDb reads on later cars, which these model years did not answer (a 2016 E-Class answered at 0x7E5 with a reply on 0x7E8, not 0x7ED, which this profile does not model); the interior units behind the central gateway, for which no source opened gives identifiers. W221, W166, R172 and the other cars of this era are not in either source. Treat every row as unconfirmed until obd-read probe shows the unit answering.
name: mercedes-w204-w212
description: Mercedes-Benz C-Class W204, GLK X204 and E-Class W212, powertrain units

engine.source: OBDb response records: a 2014 model-year C-Class (https://github.com/OBDb/Mercedes-Benz-C-Class/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2014/command_support.yaml) and a 2014 model-year E-Class (https://github.com/OBDb/Mercedes-Benz-E-Class/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2014/command_support.yaml) answered 22 2017, 22 2030, 22 2071 and 22 2095 sent to 0x7E0 with replies on 0x7E8; OBDb's generations put those years in W204 and W212. A 2012 GLK (https://github.com/OBDb/Mercedes-Benz-GLK-Class/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2012/command_support.yaml) answered none of them. Service 22 is not in this tool's KWP2000 allowlist, so these replies do not show which protocol or session the unit takes. Not read from a car by this project.

tcm.source: D_RQ_TCM 0x7E1 and D_RS_TCM 0x7E9 in lib/egs53_ecus/can_data.txt in rnd-ash/ultimate-nag52-fw (https://github.com/rnd-ash/ultimate-nag52-fw/blob/dev/lib/egs53_ecus/can_data.txt), a database its header says was parsed from 204_POWERTRAIN_SB.dat, the W204 powertrain sub-bus; OBDb response records: a 2012 GLK (https://github.com/OBDb/Mercedes-Benz-GLK-Class/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2012/command_support.yaml) answered the KWP2000 local identifier reads 21 30 and 21 34 on 0x7E9, and a 2014 E-Class (https://github.com/OBDb/Mercedes-Benz-E-Class/blob/main/tests/test_cases/2014/command_support.yaml) answered 22 0230 and 22 0234 but not 21 30 or 21 34. Not read from a car by this project.

No response record found. Not read from a car.
